name: Chatwith
task: Website or Shopify chat & FAQ deflection
summary: No-code AI agent builder that trains a support chatbot on your website, docs, files and connected apps, answers customers on your site, WhatsApp, Slack or Telegram, collects leads and escalates to a person; priced by message credits.
best_for: small and mid-sized businesses, SaaS teams and agencies that want an AI agent trained on their website, docs and connected apps to answer customer questions, collect leads and hand over to a person, at a low entry price
skip_if: you need a full help desk with ticketing and a team inbox rather than an answer bot, your traffic is unpredictable and you want a refund route, or you need phone support on a small plan
honest_knock: The real price depends on credits, and the conversation estimates assume five replies at one credit each, which the page itself says varies with the model and conversation length. Fees are non-refundable under the terms, and Starter shows no trial. The gap between Hobby at $19 and Standard at $99 is steep, so small sites may end up buying credit add-ons. Support on the two cheapest plans is community only. The agreement falls under German law. The testimonials and time-saved figures on the site are Chatwith's own. In our own test on 21 October 2026 it answered nine of ten questions correctly from 177 characters of training text and said 'I do not know' to one it could not know, but contradicted itself once ('No. ... so it is still covered') and left our last question at 'Not sent'.

pricing.notes: (read 2026-10-13 in a live browser on chatwith.tools/pricing and in the terms at chatwith.tools/terms) Four plans in US dollars, excluding taxes, with annual billing at ten times the monthly price. Starter is $9 a month or $90 a year: 250 message credits a month, about 50 conversations by the page's estimate, 1 agent and 2 million training characters. Hobby is $19 a month or $190 a year with a 7-day free trial: 1,000 credits, about 200 conversations, 1 agent and 10 million characters. Standard is $99 a month or $990 a year with a trial: 10,000 credits, about 2,000 conversations, 3 agents and 20 million characters. Business is $399 a month or $3,990 a year with a trial: 40,000 credits, about 8,000 conversations, 5 agents and 50 million characters. Sources are unlimited on every plan, and MCP action calls are allowed at 250, 1,250 and 5,000 a month on the plans that include them. The conversation estimates assume five AI replies per conversation at one credit per reply, and the page says actual use varies by model and conversation length. Add-ons are $9 a month per 1,000 extra credits, $9 per 10 million training characters, $9 per extra agent and $6 per 1,000 MCP actions. Support is community on Starter and Hobby, standard on Standard and premium on Business. The terms say fees are non-refundable and payment obligations non-cancellable except as the agreement states, you can stop renewal in your account settings and keep access to the end of the period, and the agreement falls under German law with courts in Berlin.

compare_with.name: Tidio
compare_with.why: Tidio is in our dossiers too, re-verified on 10 October 2026: Starter $29 a month paid monthly for 100 billable conversations and 10 seats, with its Lyro AI agent metered separately on top. Chatwith, read on 13 October 2026, starts at $9 a month for 250 message credits, about 50 AI conversations by its own estimate, and $19 for 1,000. Chatwith is the cheaper way to put an AI answer bot on a site; Tidio is the fuller live-chat and help-desk suite where people answer alongside the AI. With the same five facts in our own tests on 21 October 2026, Tidio's Lyro answered ten of ten questions correctly and Chatwith nine of ten.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 21 October 2026 on a new account, without connecting a website or paying: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. We trained the agent on 177 characters of text about a made-up shop (the same facts as in our Tidio test), then asked five fact questions, five rephrased ones and two it could not know. Tested plan and message allowance: not established; we did not reach the dashboard.
findings: Onboarding has four steps: Train, Brand, Test and Install. Training sources are a website (with linked pages on the same domain, or a sitemap), files, text or YouTube, against a counter of '0 / 500K characters'. Our 177 characters of text were trained in about 10 to 20 seconds.
The dashboard only opens after the onboarding: going to the app sent us back to the get-started steps. The first sign-in magic link returned 'INVALID_TOKEN'; a second one worked.

The guardrails slider starts on 'Max (default): Most sophisticated', which refuses off-topic questions and answers in the user's language; Chatwith warns that 'customizing or overriding the guardrails is difficult'.
All five fact questions were answered correctly, and four of the five rephrased ones, such as 'No. The Lila-17 is purple.' when we asked whether it was red.

Asked whether a fault after one month was covered by the 37-day warranty, it answered 'No. The Lila-17 warranty is 37 days, so it is still covered after one month.': it starts with no and ends with yes.

Asked about Sunday opening, which our text did not cover, it said 'I do not know the answer to this question.' and made nothing up. Our last question, on return costs, stayed at 'Not sent. Retry', also after a retry; we did not find out why.
The test chat made suggestion buttons from the knowledge itself (Product, Color, Pickup, Warranty) and shows 'Powered by Chatwith'.
